选自《柳宗元集》卷十七(中华书局1979 年版)。 橐(tuó)驼,即骆驼。郭橐驼因驼背而得名。 **郭橐驼,不知始何名。病偻[1],隆然[2]伏行[3],有类橐驼者,故乡人号之“驼”。驼闻之曰:“甚善。名我固当[4]。”因舍其名,亦自谓“橐驼”云。 其乡曰丰乐乡,在长安西。驼业种树[5],凡长安豪富人为观游[6]及卖果[7]者,皆争迎取养[8]。视驼所种树,或移徙[9],无不活;且硕茂[10],早实以蕃[11]。他植者虽窥伺效慕[12],莫能如也。 有问之,对曰:“橐驼非能使木寿且孳[13]也,能顺木之天[14],以致其性[15]焉尔。凡植木之性[16],其本[17]欲舒,其培[18]欲平,其土欲故[19],其筑[20]欲密。既然已[21],勿动勿虑[22],去不复顾[23]。其莳[24]也若子[25],其置也若弃[26],则其天者全而其性得矣。故吾不害其长而已,非有能硕茂之也;不抑耗其实[27]而已,非有能早而蕃之也。他植者则不然。根拳[28]而土易[29],其培之也,若不过焉则不及[30]。 苟有能反是者,则又爱之太恩[31],忧之太勤。旦视而暮抚,已去而复顾。甚者,爪其肤以验其生枯[32],摇其本以观其疏密[33],而木之性日以离[34]矣。虽曰爱之,其实害之;虽曰忧之,其实仇之;故不我若[35]也。吾又何能为哉[36] !” 问者曰:“以子之道,移之官理[37],可乎?”驼曰:“我知种树而已,理,非吾业也。然吾居乡,见长人者[38]好烦其令[39],若甚怜焉[40],而卒以祸[41]。旦暮吏来而呼曰:‘官命促尔耕,勖尔植[42],督尔获,早缫而绪[43],早织而缕[44],字而幼孩[45],遂而鸡豚[46]。’鸣鼓而聚之,击木[47]而召之。吾小人[48]辍飧饔以劳吏[49]者,且不得暇,又何以蕃吾生而安吾性耶[50] ?故病且怠[51]。若是,则与吾业者其亦有类乎?” 问者曰:“嘻,不亦善夫!吾问养树,得养人术。”传其事以为官戒也。** 本文寓意深刻,重在因事明理、针砭时弊。阅读时要注意体会文章融叙事说理于一体、婉而多讽的写法,把握对举、类比的说理方式。 这篇文章采用了传记的常见写法,从郭橐驼的名字由来、乡里职业、本领特长写起,重点记述他的两段话。阅读这部分内容,注意思考郭橐驼与“他植者”在种树方面的根本不同,郭橐驼所说的“顺木之天”与“植木之性”之间的关系等。把这些问题理解透了,才能真正领会文中的道理。 柳宗元是一位关注现实的文学家,《种树郭橐驼传》有着很强的现实针对性。文中由种树之道“移之官理”,借郭橐驼之口指出“长人者”政令频出的危害,批评了当时的弊政。这种“文章合为时而著”的创作态度,至今还值得学习和提倡。 古代汉语的人称代词较为丰富。第一人称常用“吾”“我”“余”“予”,第二人称常用“女(汝)”“尔”“而”“若”“乃”,第三人称常用“其”“彼”“之”。 [color=red]〔若子〕像对待孩子那样。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔其置也若弃〕意思是,种完后就像丢弃了一样不再管它。置,放下。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔抑耗其实〕损伤它的果实。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔拳〕拳曲,伸展不开。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔土易〕土换成了新的。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔若不过焉则不及〕(培土)如果不是多了,就是不够。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔爱之太恩〕这里指养护太过。恩,宠爱。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔爪其肤以验其生枯〕用指甲抠树皮来察看它是活着还是枯死了。爪,指甲,用作动词,用指甲抠、掐。肤,指树皮。生枯,生死。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔疏密〕指土的松紧。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔离〕背离。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔不我若〕不如我,比不上我。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔吾又何能为哉〕意思是,我又有什么特别的能耐呢?[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔官理〕做官治民。理,治。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔长(zhǎng)人者〕做官的。长,统治、治理。人,民。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔好烦其令〕喜好多发政令。烦,繁多。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔若甚怜焉〕好像很怜爱百姓的样子。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔卒以祸〕到头来因此害了他们。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔勖尔植〕勉励你们种植。勖,勉励。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔早缫(sāo)而绪〕早早地煮茧抽丝。缫,把蚕茧浸在热水里抽出蚕丝。而,你们的。绪,丝头。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔缕〕线。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔字而幼孩〕养育好你们的小孩。字,养育。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔遂而鸡豚〕喂养好你们的鸡和猪。遂,成、养好。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔木〕这里指木梆。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔吾小人〕我们小民。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔辍飧(sūn)饔(yōng)以劳吏〕中断吃饭来慰劳官吏。飧,晚饭。饔,早饭。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔又何以蕃吾生而安吾性耶〕又怎么能使我们人口增多、生活安定呢?蕃,使繁盛。[/color] ↩︎ [color=red]〔故病且怠〕所以困苦并且疲倦。病,困苦。[/color] ↩︎

This is a fascinating passage from 柳宗元 (Liu Zongyuan)'s famous work 《种树郭橐驼传》(“The Story of Guo橐驼, the Tree Planter”). Let’s break down how this passage uses narrative and reasoning, as well as some examples of ancient Chinese pronouns: 1. Narrative and Reasoning: Narrative: The passage starts by introducing 郭橐驼 (Guo Tuo Tuo), a man whose real name is unknown. He suffered from kyphosis, causing his back to hunch and resemble a camel’s hump. This earned him the nickname “橐驼” (Tuótuó, meaning “camel hump”). Reasoning: Instead of feeling ashamed, Guo Tuo Tuo readily accepts this nickname. The line “甚善。名我固当” (“Excellent. This name is indeed fitting.”) reveals his self-acceptance and indifference to societal standards. This acceptance of his physical difference becomes a subtle critique of those who judge based on appearances. 2. Rhetorical Devices: 对举 (Dui Ju - Antithesis): The passage uses contrasting descriptions to highlight Guo Tuo Tuo’s physical condition: “病偻” (bent over) vs. “隆然” (protruding), “伏行” (hunched walking) vs. “橐驼” (camel’s hump). This emphasizes his unusual physique. 类比 (Lei Bi - Analogy): The entire passage relies on the analogy between Guo Tuo Tuo and a camel. This comparison is not meant to be mocking but serves as a metaphor for his resilience and strength, qualities he later demonstrates in his exceptional tree-planting abilities. 3. Ancient Chinese Pronouns: The passage itself doesn’t use many pronouns, but here are some examples common in Classical Chinese and their modern equivalents: Classical Chinese Modern Chinese English Example 吾 (wú) 我 (wǒ) I/me 吾闻之 (I heard it) 汝 (rǔ) 你 (nǐ) you 汝何以知之? (How do you know?) 其 (qí) 他/她/它/他们/她们/它们 (tā/tāmen) he/she/it/they 其人已去 (He has already left) 此 (cǐ) 这 (zhè) this 此事甚难 (This matter is very difficult) 彼 (bǐ) 那 (nà) that 彼处甚远 (That place is very far) 皆 (jiē) 都 (dōu) all 众人皆知 (Everyone knows) In conclusion, this seemingly simple passage from “The Story of Guo Tuo Tuo, the Tree Planter” is rich in meaning. It masterfully blends narrative with subtle social commentary, using rhetorical devices to paint a vivid picture of a unique individual and challenge conventional thinking.

“早实以蕃”的“以”如何解释 @Creative

In the phrase “早实以蕃” (zǎo shí yǐ fán) from the passage, the “以” (yǐ) functions as a conjunction meaning “and” or “and thus”. Here’s a breakdown: 早实 (zǎo shí): Means “early fruiting” or “bearing fruit early”. 蕃 (fán): Means “abundant” or “plentiful”. 以 (yǐ): Connects the two parts of the phrase to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship or a simultaneous occurrence. Therefore, “早实以蕃” can be translated as: “Bears fruit early and abundantly.” “Fruits early, and thus is plentiful.” “It bears fruit early and is therefore abundant.” The “以” emphasizes that the early fruiting leads to or is accompanied by an abundance of fruit. It highlights the positive outcome of Guo Tuo Tuo’s tree-planting methods. This use of “以” as a conjunction is common in Classical Chinese. It often connects two verbs or adjectives to express a causal or consequential relationship.

在《种树郭橐驼传》中,“早实以蕃” (zǎo shí yǐ fán) 中的“以” (yǐ) 是一个连词,相当于现代汉语中的“并且”或“因而”。 具体解释如下: 早实 (zǎo shí): 指的是“结果早”。 蕃 (fán): 指的是“果实多”。 以 (yǐ): 连接前后两个部分,表示因果关系或同时发生。 因此,“早实以蕃”可以翻译为: “结果早并且多。” “结果早,因而果实很多。” “它结果早,所以果实很丰富。” 这里的“以”强调了结果早导致了或伴随着果实多,突出了郭橐驼种树方法的良好效果。 在古汉语中,“以”作连词的用法很常见,它经常连接两个动词或形容词,表示因果或顺承关系。

This is a fascinating passage from 柳宗元 (Liu Zongyuan)'s famous work 《种树郭橐驼传》(“The Story of Guo橐驼, the Tree Planter”). Let’s break down how this passage uses narrative and reasoning, as well as some examples of ancient Chinese pronouns: 1. Narrative and Reasoning: Narrative: The passage starts by introducing 郭橐驼 (Guo Tuo Tuo), a man whose real name is unknown. He suffered from kyphosis, causing his back to hunch and resemble a camel’s hump. This earned him the nickname “橐驼” (Tuótuó, meaning “camel hump”). Reasoning: Instead of feeling ashamed, Guo Tuo Tuo readily accepts this nickname. The line “甚善。名我固当” (“Excellent. This name is indeed fitting.”) reveals his self-acceptance and indifference to societal standards. This acceptance of his physical difference becomes a subtle critique of those who judge based on appearances. 2. Rhetorical Devices: 对举 (Dui Ju - Antithesis): The passage uses contrasting descriptions to highlight Guo Tuo Tuo’s physical condition: “病偻” (bent over) vs. “隆然” (protruding), “伏行” (hunched walking) vs. “橐驼” (camel’s hump). This emphasizes his unusual physique. 类比 (Lei Bi - Analogy): The entire passage relies on the analogy between Guo Tuo Tuo and a camel. This comparison is not meant to be mocking but serves as a metaphor for his resilience and strength, qualities he later demonstrates in his exceptional tree-planting abilities. 3. (How do you know?) 其 (qí) 他/她/它/他们/她们/它们 (tā/tāmen) he/she/it/they 其人已去 (He has already left) 此 (cǐ) 这 (zhè) this 此事甚难 (This matter is very difficult) 彼 (bǐ) 那 (nà) that 彼处甚远 (That place is very far) 皆 (jiē) 都 (dōu) all 众人皆知 (Everyone knows) In conclusion, this seemingly simple passage from “The Story of Guo Tuo Tuo, the Tree Planter” is rich in meaning. It masterfully blends narrative with subtle social commentary, using rhetorical devices to paint a vivid picture of a unique individual and challenge conventional thinking.

In the phrase “早实以蕃” (zǎo shí yǐ fán) from the passage, the “以” (yǐ) functions as a conjunction meaning “and” or “and thus”. Here’s a breakdown: 早实 (zǎo shí): Means “early fruiting” or “bearing fruit early”. 蕃 (fán): Means “abundant” or “plentiful”. 以 (yǐ): Connects the two parts of the phrase to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship or a simultaneous occurrence. Therefore, “早实以蕃” can be translated as: “Bears fruit early and abundantly.” “Fruits early, and thus is plentiful.” “It bears fruit early and is therefore abundant.” The “以” emphasizes that the early fruiting leads to or is accompanied by an abundance of fruit. It highlights the positive outcome of Guo Tuo Tuo’s tree-planting methods. This use of “以” as a conjunction is common in Classical Chinese. It often connects two verbs or adjectives to express a causal or consequential relationship.

在《种树郭橐驼传》中,“早实以蕃” (zǎo shí yǐ fán) 中的“以” (yǐ) 是一个连词,相当于现代汉语中的“并且”或“因而”。 具体解释如下: 早实 (zǎo shí): 指的是“结果早”。 蕃 (fán): 指的是“果实多”。 以 (yǐ): 连接前后两个部分,表示因果关系或同时发生。 因此,“早实以蕃”可以翻译为: “结果早并且多。” “结果早,因而果实很多。” “它结果早,所以果实很丰富。” 这里的“以”强调了结果早导致了或伴随着果实多,突出了郭橐驼种树方法的良好效果。 在古汉语中,“以”作连词的用法很常见,它经常连接两个动词或形容词,表示因果或顺承关系。
